# Correction writer authority fixture

Source authored and independently reviewable; **all execution UNRUN**. No source submission, push, publication, application check, database activation or live reconciliation is authorized by these files. The user holds publication until the protected pipeline is ready. Source review and an authored assertion do not establish that assertion passed.

The full candidate retains components1–35 byte-for-byte, including component34's original writer preimage. Only additive36 installs the owner successor and private exact-intent authority. This fixture does not patch a writer, adopt old intent, replay a financial operation under a new linkage or change payment semantics.

## Main acceptance interface

The root runner loads the actual captured full catalog, existing supplements and `catalog-bootstrap.sql` first. That independently owned bootstrap requires the original retained metadata, then adds exactly18 captured secondary indexes (13 ledger and five incident), seven ledger storage options and six schema-local default ACL entries. It changes no financial rows or trigger/function bodies. Existing global default ACLs remain a separately observed authority boundary.

The legacy call also requires the retained chip-store policy rows. Their exact source is `tournament-fee-lifecycle/full-lifecycle-seed.sql` line3; full-weekly `seed-registry.sql` does not contain them. Root loads `captured-store-policy.sql` once before the predecessor call. Later it loads `lifecycle-seed-after-activation.sql`, the exact original byte suffix starting at line4, at the former lifecycle-seed position after activation. The original full lifecycle seed stays byte-identical; its unrelated synthetic tournament book does not move across candidate guards. `source-provenance.json` records the exact prefix/suffix relationship. If this ordering cannot pass the unchanged candidate guards, qualification must stop; no fixture trigger may be disabled to make the legacy call pass.

Use **one psql connection**, preserving temporary inputs, through:

1. `legacy-before-candidate.sql`: original captured writer and origin triggers create a real committed ledger/key claim/invoice/two original deliveries. Only initial synthetic users, club membership, balances and linkage references are seeded under replica; no ledger/document/history row is manufactured. The actual returned receipt and complete original invoice/message/notice rows survive in temporary witnesses.
2. The complete generated36-component candidate, still using its ordinary admission guards and one transaction.
3. `legacy-replay-and-input-assertions.sql`: the original rows remain identical, no private historical intent has appeared, and real service-role replay returns exactly `legacy_correction_intent_unavailable`. Actual historical payee page/search/thread reads are identity-only; the issuer cannot obtain individual payee details. Neither audience sees old paid details through raw invoice/message/delivery/notice reads.
4. `regression.sql`: distinct successor copy of the historical34 regression. It adds private intent to the39-table snapshot, changes the obsolete changed-intent replay expectation to exact conflict, and changes NaN to exact early finite-amount refusal. The nested record-only documents, complete audiences, payee-only privacy, private/public readers, immutable claims, suppressed/mutated notices/outbox and whole-state rollback cases remain.
5. `owner-seeded-regression.sql`: includes the unchanged `owner-fixture.sql`, then `authority-regression.sql`, `deferred-overlay-regression.sql` and the legacy assertions again. The wrapper verifies original public/private/auth rows, roles and memberships after every included transaction has rolled back. Original committed legacy evidence remains intact.

Root captures accepted schema/access **after** this complete sequence, explicitly including the isolated committed legacy fixture; this is not a pristine empty database capture. `accepted-authority-supplement.sql` adds a separate read-only catalog observation for the new private table, constraints/indexes/triggers/policies, raw/effective table and column privileges (including REFERENCES and PG17 MAINTAIN), all roles' effective execute rights and exact writer/immutable-helper definitions/configuration. It never replaces one of the29 original metadata files.

## Additional authored behavior

`owner-fixture.sql` is an exact source copy of the engine owner's approved fixture. It exercises full reason and JSONB intent equality, SQL NULL versus JSON null metadata, every endpoint/scope/amount/metadata conflict, suppressed journal/incident/event/intent writes, amount/status transformations, later allowed ledger projection divergence and unchanged full-row rollback. Its original source bytes remain unchanged; orchestration supplies the real fresh and legacy inputs in the same connection.

`authority-regression.sql` invokes denied statements under actual SET LOCAL ROLE anon/authenticated/service_role, tests inherited authenticated membership, and separately proves allowed service writer/replay with two valid actors and alternate existing references. It retains both reference IDs, preserves a preexisting correction_ref, rejects replacement incident/event/private-intent projections, refuses NULL and nonfinite amounts before even looking up an invalid incident, and exercises immutable owner UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE including zero-row statements.

`deferred-overlay-regression.sql` forces a real deferred constraint failure after the writer has returned provisional success and compares every captured public/private/auth row. It also invokes the retained club-treasury/union-bank→prize-liability overlay path and checks actual escrow increments, exact replay without double overlay, unchanged wallet and mint rows, and the existing deferrable issuance exclusion for correction category. Prize-liability and outside-store corrections remain outside component34's supported document routes; these cases do not claim a new paid invoice or universal absence of escrow effects. All their test mutations roll back.

## Separate concurrent sessions

Root wires `concurrency-regression.py` as an explicit **14th fresh sequential cluster** after the prior13 full-runner phases. It requires the actual captured catalog, `catalog-bootstrap.sql`, the full36 candidate and `concurrency-setup.sql` in the `postgres` database of that new cluster. Preserved cron and candidate guards require that name; no original guard is changed. It never shares the acceptance cluster/connection. Setup atomically creates a fixture-only, owner-only marker with a fresh run UUID, database OID and postmaster start time alongside the synthetic book. Every driver connection verifies that marker and is pinned to the same UUID; restart, missing/widened marker authority or reused starting references refuse admission. `concurrency-session.sql` creates only isolated per-connection helpers and has bounded initial guard/DDL timeouts. `captured-store-policy.sql` preserves the exact existing policy INSERT for this separate database, which does not run the lifecycle seed.

The harness takes only qualified absolute psql/socket paths, a bounded port and an allowlisted disposable database name; it clears credential inheritance and uses no production secrets. Actual PostgreSQL blocker identity, not elapsed sleep, establishes each wait. The same-linkage identical and conflicting calls must retain one journal/key claim/private intent/document/delivery. A contender can receive only an exact replay/conflict or a23505 refusal naming one of the two captured key constraints. Timeouts, transport loss, other SQLSTATEs and unknown receipts fail qualification; they are never transformed into success or proof of cancellation. Subsequent exact replay and changed-intent conflict must leave every authoritative row unchanged.

Separate interleavings hold the real incident or tournament-escrow row while the original writer waits. A newly committed incident reference must survive; the existing escrow increment and correction overlay must both survive once. The harness compares the writer's complete precommit state with the final committed state, then exact replay with full-state equality. Its committed synthetic evidence must be archived before root verifies PostgreSQL stopped and destroys the disposable cluster. Stopping a psql client alone does not prove backend retirement; the root harness owns that separate lifecycle check.

## Provenance and limits

The exact source pins and copy relationships are listed in `source-provenance.json`. Historical `correction-document-authority/regression.sql` remains SHA256 `f70b287534ee6024469629a18fd38cb4074f528e906808c5bf6ebdb1464091f1`. The copied owner fixture remains SHA256 `26f460362d5fba69998bedb1927d1ea69e668c5d36f6c056e484704687319fe9`.

All row snapshots preserve IDs, timestamps and previous receipts; sequence allocations intentionally are not rolled-back row state. Isolated session helpers that expose snapshots are fixture-only and do not alter production RLS/grants. SET ROLE from a postgres-owned fixture exercises effective SQL role behavior but is not a genuine non-owner provider/JWT session matrix; `ca_can_view_club` has an owner-session bypass. Actual provider-session privacy, non-owner union overseer audience, native deparser/ACL/default behavior, complete concurrent interleavings, provider delivery, installation and live reconciliation remain unqualified until separately executed and observed. No finite set of fixtures establishes that every future transaction can never fail.
